title: The Unwritten Atlas
premise: In the winter of 1862, Ivo Voss keeps the light at Cape Merren and tells himself the war, the famine, and the courts belong to a world he left behind when his wife died. A half-drowned stranger washes ashore carrying letters in the handwriting of Aldous Renwick — a reformer officially executed two years ago, whose 'confession' condemned forty innocent men. The stranger is Renwick's daughter, alive under a false name, and she needs the letters carried through three military checkpoints to a tribunal that convenes in six weeks. Ivo, who once forged documents for a cause he swore he'd abandoned, must decide whether his invisibility was cowardice or survival; by the final chapter, having lost the lighthouse itself to fire and suspicion, he delivers the atlas of evidence at the cost of his anonymity, choosing truth over the quiet life he built from grief.
about_author: Cyrus Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing smugglers' letters and coastal court records before turning to fiction. He writes from a house within sight of a decommissioned lighthouse, where he claims the fog does half the editing.

chapters.title: The Light That Answers No One
chapters.summary: Ivo Voss tends the Cape Merren light alone, narrating his rigid routines as armor against grief and history alike. When supply boat pilot Tam mentions rumors of tribunals on the mainland, Ivo shuts the conversation down. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the comfort and hollowness of deliberate invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Sea Surrenders
chapters.summary: After a violent squall, Ivo finds a woman half-buried in wrack below the tower — Mara, feverish, clutching an oilskin packet she refuses to release even unconscious. He recognizes the seal's wax impression and feels his stomach drop. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: A Hand I Buried
chapters.summary: Delirious, Mara murmurs a name: Aldous Renwick. Ivo examines the packet's letters and knows the handwriting intimately — he once forged documents alongside Renwick before the crackdown. The man executed for treason wrote these pages last month. POV: Ivo, with flashback. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Daughter of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Mara recovers enough to explain: her father lives in hiding; the letters prove the confession that condemned forty men was forged — by someone inside the movement. She must reach the tribunal at Corvenne in five weeks, but soldiers watch every road. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: desperate trust extended to a stranger.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Mara lays out the route: the ferry at Saltbridge, the garrison town of Halloway, the mountain pass at Verrin Ford. Each checkpoint searches for a woman traveling alone. Ivo argues it's impossible; she asks what he did during the purges. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: accusation cracking open old shame.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo admits he forged the movement's papers years ago, then vanished after his wife Elise died — some say betrayed, some say broken. Mara realizes he can pass checkpoints precisely because no one remembers him. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Lies
chapters.summary: They pose as brother and sister delivering lamp oil to mainland buyers. Ivo coaches Mara on their invented family, unnerved by how easily lying returns to him. At Saltbridge they see wanted notices: not for Renwick, but for 'the Keeper's accomplice.' POV: Mara. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Question
chapters.summary: At Saltbridge checkpoint, a sharp-eyed sergeant named Brack chats amiably while his men search the cart. Ivo's forged transit papers hold — until Brack asks why a lighthouse keeper travels in storm season. Ivo answers with a lie about his dead wife's grave. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: terror mastered, barely.

chapters.title: Letters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Crossing at night, Mara reads Ivo one letter aloud: Renwick names the forger of the false confession — initials I.V. Ivo goes cold; either his old mentor is framing him, or warning him. POV: both, tense dialogue. Emotional beat: loyalty and suspicion colliding.

chapters.title: Halloway's Bright Cages
chapters.summary: Halloway garrison is festive, distracted by a visiting colonel — but Brack has telegraphed ahead. The pair hide in a cooper's cellar belonging to Nell Ashby, an old comrade of Ivo's who never forgave him for disappearing. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: confronting the cost of his vanishing.

chapters.title: Nell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nell agrees to help only if Ivo carries her own testimony — a ledger of the disappeared — adding weight and risk to the packet. She also reveals Brack was once a movement courier turned informer. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: bitterness yielding to solidarity.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Dinner
chapters.summary: To divert the garrison, Nell engineers an invitation for Ivo — posing as a wine merchant — to dine at the colonel's table. He endures an evening beside the very officers hunting him, hearing them discuss the tribunal they intend to discredit. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, dangerous thrill of proximity.

chapters.title: Fire Alarm
chapters.summary: Their exit is nearly discovered; Mara creates a diversion that goes wrong, and a stable burns. They escape Halloway at dawn but leave witnesses and a description behind. Mara blames herself; Ivo, unexpectedly, defends her. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: guilt met, for once, with grace.

chapters.title: Verrin Ford in Snow
chapters.summary: The mountain pass is closed by early snow — the third checkpoint becomes a frozen trap. They shelter in a shepherd's hut where Mara reveals she isn't Renwick's daughter but his courier and protégée; the real daughter died in prison. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: identity stripped to its truest form.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Pass
chapters.summary: Brack, anticipating the route, waits at Verrin Ford with soldiers. But he hesitates when Ivo invokes a shared night years ago when Brack's life was saved by forged papers. Brack lets the cart pass — then fires a warning shot, torn between debt and duty. POV: Brack. Emotional beat: a compromised man's agony.

chapters.title: What Brack Knows
chapters.summary: Brack catches up alone at night, off the record: the forger of Renwick's false confession is Judge Ellery Mott, who will preside over the tribunal itself. Delivering the letters means delivering them into Mott's hands. POV: Brack. Emotional beat: the ground giving way beneath the mission.

chapters.title: Renwick Alive
chapters.summary: Following Brack's cryptic directions, they find Aldous Renwick hiding in a quarry chapel — alive, ill, and despairing, convinced his evidence is worthless if Mott controls the court. Ivo, the forger, sees another way: make the truth undeniable publicly. POV: Renwick. Emotional beat: hope rebuilt from wreckage.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Atlas
chapters.summary: Ivo proposes printing excerpts of the letters in Corvenne's newspapers before the tribunal opens, forcing Mott to act honestly or openly destroy himself. Renwick resists — exposure means death. Mara sides with Ivo. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the invisible man volunteering to be seen.

chapters.title: Night of the Presses
chapters.summary: In Corvenne, using Nell's contacts and Ivo's forgery skills, they set type by candlelight. Soldiers raid the print shop as the first sheets roll; Renwick stays behind to hold the door, telling Ivo, 'History happens to people who show up for it.' POV: Mara. Emotional beat: sacrifice accepted without melodrama.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Opens
chapters.summary: Corvenne wakes to broadsheets bearing Renwick's handwriting and Mott's signature on the forged confession. The tribunal chamber erupts; Mott recuses himself under public roar. Ivo testifies openly as the former forger, naming names, surrendering his anonymity forever. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: terror and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ashes at Cape Merren
chapters.summary: Retribution comes quietly: soldiers burn the lighthouse records and Ivo is dismissed, his post given away. Standing in the ruins of his routine, he feels lighter than he has since Elise died. Mara offers him work archiving testimony for the restored court. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Light
chapters.summary: Spring. Ivo and Mara travel the coast collecting the disappeared's stories into a published atlas of testimony — the book the title promises. At the darkened Cape Merren tower, he lights a single lantern in the window anyway, for anyone still finding their way. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution — justice as ongoing work, not ending.
